pr_title: Fix scaling last bone length with negative scales
pr_body:
Fixes: #80643 

Change to use absolute value.  

**EDIT**:
I was trying to maintain the logic "use the lower value to define the length of the last bone", but I don't think this the right way.  
The user always want to see how much the bone is scaled in any direction, so why use the lower value?  

No change to scale:
![Bones with all scales 1](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/9352894/debcc54a-eea5-4a2e-9138-ec791314edf0)  

Current behaviour when scaling X to 3:
![Bones with X scaled to 3, current behavior](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/9352894/407ecb90-296b-4bc7-887f-fe5c350d8b7a)  

Propose change:
![Bones with X scaled to 3, propose behavior](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/9352894/11094488-de93-40bf-8ada-5ecdbdbf089a)  

This also helps with #76087, in this issue we can see that saving calls this functions to redraw bones. Current behavior:  

- Before the user save, they are scaled using both X and Y axis.  
- After the user save, it redraw only using the lower value from scale.  

Note: Changing this would only help with the **last** bone.

issue_context.title: The last Bone2D in the chain will scale incorrectly
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.2.dev3.official [013e8e3af]

### System information

Ubuntu 23.04 x86_64

### Issue description

When scaling the last Bone2D from the chain, there is a specific case where the bone length will be more than expected.  

The main logic is to use the lower value from scale `MIN(get_global_scale().x, get_global_scale().y)`:  
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c495eb5102278a110c14bbffbf833ed436d1594d/scene/2d/skeleton_2d.cpp#L328  

But this can go wrong when the lower value is negative, attention for (-1, 3) and (1, -3):  
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/9352894/257498ad-e2d4-41a0-ba98-04e315b2df63)  

**Note**: This can easily be fixed by getting the absolute value from scale.  
```cpp
rel = Vector2(cos(angle_to_use), sin(angle_to_use)) * (length * MIN(ABS(get_global_scale().x), ABS(get_global_scale().y)));
```  

**Note 2**: (1, -3) and (-1, 3) are equal after saving the project because the project reload information from transforms and the (-1, 3) is convert to (1, -3).  

### Steps to reproduce

- Create a scene with Node2D as root
- Add a Skeleton2D
- Add a Bone2D
- Scale Bone2D by (1, -3)

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A

review_comments:
```suggestion
		rel = Vector2(cos(angle_to_use), sin(angle_to_use)) * length * get_global_scale();
```
I see that using MIN is causing incorrect results.

But I think it is odd in this PR why it needs abs(). I think simply removing the MIN would be sufficient, as this would cause problems that would make it impossible to set negative scale the end bones. If the value needs to be absolute for IK, then it should use abs()  in the IK calculation not here.

It seems that the shape is draw AFTER the node draw itself.  
Which means that shape is not affected by the absolute value of the node scale, only by the sign.  

If you were to scale Y negatively without `abs()`:   

[Screencast from 2024-01-10 16-00-02.webm](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/9352894/49f8a438-1f19-4da6-8c33-5253051cc3de)  

This may also be the reason for SkeletonModificationLookAt not pointing to the right location when Y is negative:  

[Screencast from 2024-01-10 16-01-43.webm](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/9352894/c5c1eab4-5946-429b-af88-f020dccdde97)

**Note**: `get_global_scale` always give a positve X, this is why scaling X doesn't show us any problem (https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node2d.html#class-node2d-property-scale).

The flip in -Y probably involves a normalization problem. It may be a specification. Do you have any ideas in this part @reduz? Since I remember having a similar discussion before in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/69202.

However, at least in SkeletonModificationLookAt calculation, it should be resolved in SkeletonModificationLookAt, and it should not be correct way to force abs() to fix it here.

> However, at least in SkeletonModificationLookAt calculation, it should be resolved in SkeletonModificationLookAt, and it should not be correct way to force abs() to fix it here.

I agree, but i'm not sure if is SkeletonModificationLookAt fault in this case.  
Only the bone draw seems to be wrong because node and child nodes are actually looking at the at target.

[Screencast from 2024-01-10 17-17-19.webm](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/9352894/35833bc1-6106-4acc-a3d7-a7ee6e0d35ba)
If only gizmo is strange, it could be a problem with Skeleton2DGizmo. It would be recommendable to check if there is no problem in skeleton_2d_editor_plugin.cpp.

Skeleton2DGizmo doesn't exist in Godot (only Skeleton3DGizmo).  
skeleton_2d_editor_plugin.cpp only seems to have the logic to rest & overwrite rest pose.  

skeleton_2d.cpp comment indicates that we are looking at the right file:  
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/26b1fd0d842fa3c2f090ead47e8ea7cd2d6515e1/scene/2d/skeleton_2d.cpp#L191-L192  

I believe that this PR is in the right place for the gizmo drawing logic.

I looked into it, and I think the gizmo direction mismatch from axes is a specification. Even if there is no negative scale, the BoneAngle will generate a visual offset of the gizmo. In other words, if we force Polygon2DEditor to draw Gizmo on X-axis, Bone Angle will not work.

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/61938263/f68631bb-c862-4fcf-9d10-c8d23eebd7fc)

Finally, the LookAt issue is that it just doesn't take that offset into account; It seems to work for directing only X axis.

> You should see `Polygon2DEditor`.

Still need to see :laughing: 

> I looked into it, and I think the gizmo direction mismatch from axes is a specification. Even if there is no negative scale, the BoneAngle will generate a visual offset of the gizmo.

Sorry, I failed understand your point.  
In my case I'm always using BoneAngle 0º, so the expected is to match X-axis.  
I do rotate the Node rotation, but when using BoneAngle 0º this would means matching X-axis. Right?  

> In other words, if we force Polygon2DEditor to draw Gizmo on X-axis, Bone Angle will not work.

What you mean by forcing it to draw Gizmo on X-axis?  

---

What I understand is right now is:
- Gizmo is drawn every frame
- Gizmo is not a child of Bone2D so it's not affected by it scales
- We need to add scale when drawing
- Right now we are getting the lower scale
  - Which brings the weird behavior when one scale is negative
- We use absolute to calculate the correct the length
  - `Vector2(cos(angle_to_use), sin(angle_to_use)) * length * get_global_scale().abs()`
    - `Vector2(cos(angle_to_use), sin(angle_to_use))` is the vector direction
    - `length * get_global_scale().abs()` is the length scaled (a number)
      - If we do **not** use the absolute here
        - `length * get_global_scale()` this will give us a vector and I have no idea why we would multiple direction by a vector.

Correct me if I'm seeing something wrong.

> In my case I'm always using BoneAngle 0º, so the expected is to match X-axis.

That is the case that BoneAngle is zero **and the scale is isotropic**.

I am not so familiar with the Bone2D specification, but it seems that if the scales are not isotropic, they are implicitly representing the BoneAngle.

The fundamental problem is that Gizmo2D doesn't have the ability to distort axes like Gizmo3D, but if BoneAngle is non-zero (even if it is due to non-isotropic scales), the bone is not needed aligned with the X axis, so the offset should not be corrected by `abs()`.

In other words, there is nothing wrong with bone / Gizmo, as it does not need to match X-axis all the time. So what needs to be fixed is not Gizmo, but LookAt. It means that LookAt must make the modified axis (which takes into account BoneAngle and non-isotropic scale) point to the target, not make the X-axis point to the target.

I don't understand enough about the subject... I need to study  

![sad gif - konosuba](https://c.tenor.com/m7zC_iHi-r0AAAAC/tenor.gif)

Oh, sorry. I looked at the more details and may have misunderstood. It looked like the anisotropic Scale was acting strangely, but in fact it may just be that LookAt was ignoring the Auto calculation setting and setting the BoneAngle. Well, in any case, I believe there is a bug in LookAt.
Seems Bone Angle has a different issue and seems to be due to the fact that Auto Calculate Length and Angle is unstable. I send PR for that https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/91759.

After further investigation, I see that the abs() is necessary here because there is reverse rotation, but I think the original implementation which needs reverse rotation was odd to begin with.

I have reviewed the implementation in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/91731, so would appreciate your testing. We shouldn't need abs() there.
I did my best to find some error, but it seems to be okay.

This PR is attempting to give scale to `length` and could probably be solved by changing how `length` is calculated: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/83397#discussion_r1426076290

(just an observation, no change should be made in this PR)
